title: Shape catalog
description: Validates curated/shapes/shapes.json -- the authoring-time shape catalog. Logged as missing since 2026-07-15 in docs/schema/shape-catalog.md ('shapes.schema.json -- not yet written as a file'); written 2026-07-22. It covers the catalog's own envelope: that each shape has an id, a slot list, and a template. The template's INTERNALS are deliberately not re-specified here -- they are $defs/shape_template in api-schema.json, which workflow/formal/validate.py's validate_shape_template() already enforces on every shape at test time, and duplicating that structure in a second file is exactly the kind of copy that goes stale.

id.description: Dotted shape identifier, '<family>.<name>' (e.g. 'collective.one_to_all_uniform', 'rma.put'). Referenced by a proposal's shape_ref; must be unique across the catalog, which workflow/validate/test_curated.py checks.

$comment.description: Why this shape exists rather than being folded into a neighbour, and any notes on its design. Written for every shape minted after a near-miss was rejected, per 'a wrong fit is worse than an honest gap'. Absorbed the former provenance `notes` on 2026-07-22.

slots.description: The bindable holes in the template. A binding supplies one value per non-optional slot; expansion substitutes it for the matching '{{slot_name}}' token.

name.description: Slot name, referenced in the template as '{{name}}'.

kind.description: What kind of value the slot accepts. Closed vocabulary: a new kind is new authoring-time vocabulary and needs the same justification as a new shape.

optional.description: Whether a binding may omit this slot.

template.description: The semantics.formal skeleton with '{{slot}}' tokens in place of bound values. Structure per $defs/shape_template in api-schema.json -- enforced there, not re-stated here.

motivated_by.description: Entry keys ('model:function_key') of the real functions this shape was derived from -- the project's design-by-concrete-example rule, recorded. Moved here from the seed file 2026-07-22 so a shape's justification travels with the shape.

cross_ppm_reusable.description: Whether the shape is confirmed shared across PPMs -- the reuse that justifies the catalog's complexity at all. Two spellings, both deliberate: `true` when the reuse is unqualified, and a prose qualifier when partial ('MPI only, per shape-catalog.md's own table'; 'SHMEM + NVSHMEM only -- MPI deliberately excluded'). 14 of 27 shapes carry the prose form; a bare `false` would lose the distinction between 'not reusable' and 'reusable across this subset, for this reason'.
